daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The government is reviewing the Anti-Corruption Law to align with the UN Convention Against Corruption, with Minister Yusril signaling potential changes to the definition of state financial losses. Yusril emphasized that under-invoicing and illegal fishing should be included in the corruption definition, while also using BUMN cases as examples to clarify what constitutes state losses. The review aims to expand the definition of corruption in the amended law.

  • The DPR accelerated the Asset Forfeiture Bill by forming a working committee that will continue meetings during the recess period.
  • Constitutional activists challenged the Presidential Advisory Council Law at the Constitutional Court, revealing council members' salaries and arguing the lack of a membership cap burdens the state budget.
  • Kompas reported on Gerindra and PDIP drawing closer, placing former President Jokowi at a crossroads regarding coalition dynamics.
  • Two children of the Hajj Minister resigned from expert staff positions at the Hajj Ministry.
  • Minister Maruarar reported to President Prabowo that the house renovation program increased from 45,000 to 400,000 units.
  • The Polda Jatim allegedly picked up the Unair student council president at his home over calls to demonstrate, though he was later released after his phone was seized.
  • The government prohibited BUMN officials from using official vehicles for family members.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and India launched a creative-tech corridor to boost cooperation in artificial intelligence and intellectual property. This bilateral initiative represents a significant deepening of technological ties between the two countries as Indonesia seeks to accelerate its digital transformation.

  • Indonesia and Japan are expanding people-to-people ties ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations.
  • Indonesia is seeking Asian partners to build a semiconductor ecosystem.
  • The Vice Minister of Hajj assured that Saudi Arabia is safe for umrah pilgrimages.
  • The TNI Chief and National Police Chief officially received Korpasgat command brevets and witnessed special forces demonstrations in Bandung.
  • A Kopassus officer, Letda Jihad Ahmad, died after a pistol accidentally discharged at a Kopassus warehouse.

Other

President Prabowo disbursed Rp 200 billion to tackle land and forest fires in South Sumatra, as the government intensifies efforts to combat the crisis. The BNPB deployed 14 tons of cloud seeding material to address the fires, while Kompas warned that hydrometeorological disasters are looming even as fires have not fully subsided. The South Sumatra governor demanded palm oil planted on burned land be uprooted after claiming only two hotspots remain.

  • State holding company Danantara is eyeing US$30 billion to accelerate Indonesia's industrial growth.
  • Indonesia plans to build crude oil storage facilities for direct imports, while oil prices remain at US$115 per barrel.
  • Bank Indonesia is monitoring the rupiah amid market volatility and surging oil prices, while targeting US$55 billion in local currency transactions in 2026.
  • Indonesia's Sekolah Rakyat projects have employed 97,000 workers, with Cabinet Secretary Teddy visiting a Sekolah Rakyat to sing with students and inspect dormitories.
  • Authorities foiled illegal gold exports worth Rp 61.95 billion, while the government will soon take action against illegal gold mining in Sangihe.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs formed a task force to prevent violence in Islamic boarding schools.
